findings.description: The reports_archive bucket has no server_side_side_encryption_configuration block and no bucket-level encryption default, so objects written to it (including the seeded vendor roster spreadsheet) may be stored unencrypted.
The ledger_exports bucket stores financial ledger data but declares no server-side encryption configuration, leaving objects unencrypted at rest.
The model_artifacts bucket has versioning and logging configured but no server-side encryption, so model artifacts are stored unencrypted.
The ops_runbooks bucket declares no server-side encryption configuration, so operational runbooks are stored unencrypted at rest.

The audit_trail bucket uses acl = "lcatalogopts-delivery-write" (a canned ACL granting a log-delivery group write access), which is not a valid/appropriate ACL for an audit log bucket and exposes write access to an external principal.

Because force_destroy = true is set on the audit_trail bucket, the retained audit logs and the log-target bucket for other services can be destroyed and purged without objection, undermining audit integrity.

The reports_archive bucket defines no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so account- or bucket-level policy changes could expose its contents publicly; the vendor roster object placed in it is likewise unprotected.
The ledger_exports bucket has no public access block attached, leaving the default of allowing public access via future ACLs or bucket policies.
The model_artifacts bucket has no public access block defined, so public exposure of model artifact data is not prevented at the configuration level.
The ops_runbooks bucket defines no public access block, so its contents are not protected from accidental public exposure.
The audit_trail bucket has no public access block, meaning the logging destination for other buckets could be exposed publicly.
Neither reports_archive nor ledger_exports nor ops_runbooks enable S3 access logging to the audit_trail bucket, so access to their contents is not recorded.
The reports_archive bucket does not enable versioning, so objects (including the seed vendor roster) can be overwritten or deleted irreversibly; versioning would support recovery and integrity.
The ledger_exports bucket does not enable versioning, leaving financial ledger exports overwritable and unrecoverable from accidental or malicious deletion.
The vendor roster object is uploaded without any server-side encryption, content-type, or KMS key specification, so the spreadsheet contents are stored and served unencrypted.
